name_evidence.wording: Wikivoyage town guide 'Esperance' (See/Do: museum, Great Ocean Drive, beaches); Australia's Golden Outback page headed 'Esperance' in its Esperance Coast region

proposed_destinations.name: Nullarbor Plain
proposed_destinations.coordinates_source: computed: middle of its spots' pins (bounding-box centre), per COVERAGE "centre it on the middle of its spots"

name_evidence.wording: Golden Outback page headed 'Norseman & Nullarbor'; Wikivoyage 'Nullarbor' redirects to the Eyre Highway article's 'Nullarbor Plain' section; 88,149 Wikipedia page views

proposed_destinations.reason: The Nullarbor Plain was kept but is a 200,000 km2 region, not a pinnable place (skeptic: treat it as a destination or region). Travellers say 'we're crossing the Nullarbor' and the board brands it; its WA stops (Eucla Telegraph Station, Eucla, Eyre Bird Observatory, Madura Pass, 90 Mile Straight, Eucla National Park) are its six spots. Span covers Caiguna to Eucla (about 320 km). The plain continues into South Australia (Bunda Cliffs were rejected as outside WA): an SA run would widen and recentre it. Norseman, 380 km west of Caiguna, stays standalone as the western gateway.

Its listed draws are small and some open only on request (the courthouse museum is 'call Shire for details'). A town with one source and short stops is marginal. That is the marginal combination COVERAGE sends to review (one source and a short visit). The case for keeping it is that it is a scientifically unique, quirky stop that a shire signposts for visitors.

review.reason: Rule 1: own board page naming the Mount O'Brien lookout, Mount Matilda walk, pioneer museum and spring wildflower reserves.
review.objection: Small farming town, 671 page views, one counted source; the lookout and walk are 10 km west and the wildflowers seasonal; a traveller from elsewhere goes mainly in wildflower season.

review.name: Frank Hann National Park
review.reason: Rule 1: Parks WA visitor page (wildflowers along Lake King-Norseman Road, bushwalks); open and free.
review.objection: No facilities or marked walks; the page itself says you can see it from your car on a through road, so it may be a drive-through rather than a place to stop for half an hour. One source.

review.name: Rossiter Bay
review.reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage See listing and the board's combined 'Mississippi Hill and Rossiter Bay' listing; the 1841 Eyre rescue site at the end of the coastal trail.
review.objection: Wikivoyage itself says 'the bay is not particularly exciting'; its interest is historical; could fold into Mississippi Hill or the coastal trail.

review.name: Boorabbin National Park
review.reason: Rule 1: DBCA Explore Parks page ('nature's rest stop' on the Great Eastern Highway: bushwalk among wildflowers, banksias, the old Boorabbin townsite).
review.objection: One counted source; the agency itself frames it as a leg-stretch stop on the highway.

review.name: Burtville
review.reason: Rule 1: Golden Outback board names it as a historic site of a former outback town near Laverton; a ghost town to explore, 587 page views.
review.objection: One counted source, mentioned in passing; little remains and access is by outback tracks.

review.name: Lennonville
review.reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page (Mount Magnet) names exploring the remains of abandoned settlements such as Lennonville.
review.objection: Named in passing only; little is left of the townsite, so it may not hold a visitor for half an hour (rule 2). One source.

review.name: Charles Darwin Reserve
review.reason: Rule 1: the Golden Outback Perenjori page names it (a Bush Heritage reserve of national ecological significance, 230 animal and 680 plant species, camping June-September at Samphire Campground, booked through Bush Heritage); Bush Heritage also runs guided visits.
review.objection: Open only by booking in a limited season (sources disagree: Apr-Oct or Jun-Sep); one counted source. Boundary unsure: the Shire of Perenjori is administratively Mid West, next to the coral-coast wildflower towns (Morawa, Three Springs), though the Golden Outback brand lists it under the Wheatbelt.

review.name: Culham Inlet
review.reason: Rule 1: the board's own listing: a landlocked estuary west of Hopetoun with fishing and lookouts.
review.objection: One source; mainly a fishing spot; of local appeal.

review.name: Yenyening Lakes
review.reason: Rule 1: two counted sources, Australia's Golden Outback product page and Wheatbelt Tourism's Granite Outcrops & Salt Lakes page (birdlife, water sports, photography). Boundary unsure: 32 km SE of Beverley, spanning the Beverley, Brookton and Quairading shires; Beverley is in wa-perth's Avon Valley.
review.objection: Salt lakes that need generous rain to fill; mainly a local recreation spot; may belong to wa-perth.

review.name: Baladjie Rock
review.reason: Rule 1: Central Wheatbelt Visitor Centre's Eastern Wheatbelt drive trail lists it under granite outcrops; climb for views over Baladjie Lake.
review.objection: One counted source; remote picnic and camping spot.

review.name: Lake Monjingup
review.reason: Rule 1+2: the board's own listing: a lake with a boardwalk, picnic area, bird watching and spring wildflowers.
review.objection: One counted source; a local nature reserve (Lake Monjingup Reserve) of the 'ordinary reserve near a town' kind COVERAGE leaves out unless guides feature it.

review.name: Cave Hill
review.reason: Rule 1: the Golden Outback board names Cave Hill among Coolgardie's outback nature reserves; a granite hill with caves, a camping and 4WD spot in the Great Western Woodlands.
review.objection: One counted source, 4WD access only, and no detail on what the visitor does there in the source; no DBCA page found (exploreparks 404).

review.name: Woody Lake Nature Reserve
review.reason: Rule 1+2: the board lists the Woody Lake Nature Reserve Canoe Trail, a waymarked paddle through paperbark channels.

review.name: Datjoin Rock
review.reason: Rule 1: named as a Wheatbelt Way stop near Beacon with a picnic area (guidebook, not directly read).
review.objection: Source thin and not opened directly; a minor outcrop.

review.name: Totadgin Conservation Park
review.reason: Rule 1: named only by the regional board (Merredin and Hyden & Wave Rock pages: mini wave rock, interpretive trail, picnic spot); Wikivoyage Hyden does not mention it, so effectively one counted source.

review.name: Archer Drive Lookout

review.name: Mount Short Scenic Drive

review.name: Norseman Historical Collection

review.name: Duke of Orleans Bay

notes: Western Australia has no destinations or spots in the app yet: nothing to move (existing_fixes empty). Every destination and standalone id was checked against src/data and git history (git log -S) and is new.

Pins: Overpass (overpass-api.de) was unreachable throughout, so resolve-pin.py returned HIGH only for Twilight Beach, Blue Haven Beach, Observatory Point and Esperance Stonehenge. Other pins come from a single OpenStreetMap feature of the right type found by name through Nominatim (MEDIUM) or two agreeing sources (HIGH), each recorded in coordinates_source. Town pins use the OSM locality's label point (MEDIUM; confirm the place node). 50 spots have coordinates null with needs_research ['coordinates'] and a pin_note: rerun resolve-pin.py for every spot before applying.

Never carried over (brief's wrong-coordinate list): Museum of the Goldfields, Hannans North Tourist Mine and London Bridge (Sandstone) have coordinates null; London Bridge's 370,378 views are London's and are not its score.

Hours and prices are filled only where a counted source gave them (Super Pit Lookout 7 AM - 7 PM; Gwalia 9:30 AM - 4 PM; Merredin Military Museum 10 AM - 3 PM, $10; Merredin Railway Museum 11 AM - 2 PM, $15; The Lace Place and Wave Rock Wildlife Park 9 AM - 5 PM). free: true is set only for open public places with no operator (beaches, lookouts, roadside art, town streets); national parks are left for research because DBCA charges vehicle entry at some parks.
Destination categories: Hyden, Merredin and Ravensthorpe are towns ('city'); Nullarbor Plain is 'desert'. Hyden could instead be named 'Wave Rock' (owner's call; see its reason).

Towns kept beside an attraction in them (Norseman and the Tin Camels; Laverton and the Hall of Fame; Southern Cross and the Yilgarn museum; Coolgardie and its museum; Sandstone and London Bridge; Wiluna and its gallery; Corrigin and its Dog Cemetery; Kulin and the Tin Horse Highway): each town has named draws that no kept spot covers (listed in its reason), so it is not a wrapper. Towns whose only draw was the attraction were merged (Leonora, Kambalda, Dundas). Owner may merge more.
